🎯 How can the healthcare ecosystem be transformed beyond just applying new technologies?

As part of my PhD research on DigitalTwins in Healthcare, I recently read a compelling book, "Digital Transformation in Healthcare: An Ecosystem Approach", by Prof. Panos Constantinides, which has shaped my thinking on this question. 

The book explores the complexities of digital_evolution in healthcare, highlighting several systemic challenges:

📌 Rising service costs
📌 Unclear benefits
📌 Fragmented data access and interoperability issues
📌 Siloed infrastructures and coordination challenges

These are not merely technical problems; they are structural and relational, rooted in the interconnected network of stakeholders within the healthcare ecosystem. The book emphasizes the importance of co-adoption and co-innovation to create sustainable and value-driven partnerships.

From my PhD perspective, digital twins offer an integrative approach to these challenges, leveraging real-time simulation, predictive modeling, and data harmonization to generate actionable insights, enhance coordination, and support system-wide innovation.

This book has deepened my understanding of what true digital transformation in healthcare requires:

➡️ A shift in mindset
➡️ A focus on ecosystem_wide collaboration
➡️ A rethinking of relationships, responsibilities, and value_creation.
